about: Topic map of the AP Microeconomics Course and Exam Description (effective fall 2026, no content change for 2026-27), in LevlPrep's own words from docs/apmicro-research/framework.md. Every topic title is official (Course at a Glance). Objectives and knowledge are our summaries; for 3.4 to 6.5 they come from scoring guidelines, Chief Reader Reports and standard economics (the CED text could not be read past 3.3) and say so in source.

ced.title: AP Microeconomics Course and Exam Description
ced.edition: Effective fall 2026 (6 units, 36 topics); no content change for 2026-27
ced.verification: All 36 titles and skill tags from the Course at a Glance. CED text readable for Units 1-2 and Topics 3.1-3.3. Exclusions read: indifference curves (1.6), graphing quotas (2.9). Read 2026-11-09.

bigIdeas.name: Scarcity and Markets
bigIdeas.summary: How scarcity forces choices and how markets set prices and quantities.

bigIdeas.name: Costs, Benefits, and Marginal Analysis
bigIdeas.summary: How consumers and firms compare costs and benefits at the margin.

bigIdeas.name: Production Choices and Behavior
bigIdeas.summary: How firms produce, set prices and hire in different market structures.

bigIdeas.name: Market Inefficiency and Public Policy
bigIdeas.summary: When markets fail and how policy changes outcomes.

skillNames.1.A: Describe economic concepts, principles or models
skillNames.1.B: Identify an economic concept, principle or model from an example
skillNames.1.C: Identify an economic concept, principle or model using data or calculations
skillNames.1.D: Describe similarities, differences and limitations of concepts, principles or models

skillNames.2.A: Explain how an outcome occurs or what action achieves it
skillNames.2.B: Explain outcomes with several variables or actions
skillNames.2.C: Interpret an outcome using data or calculations

skillNames.3.A: Determine an outcome using a model
skillNames.3.B: Determine the effects of changes on other markets
skillNames.3.C: Determine effects using data or calculations

skillNames.4.B: Show a specific situation on a labeled graph or visual
skillNames.4.C: Show the effect of a change on a labeled graph or visual

topics.title: Scarcity
objectives: Explain how scarcity forces trade-offs in using limited resources.
knowledge: Wants outrun the resources (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) available, so every choice gives something up.
Most resources are scarce; some, such as knowledge everyone can use at once, may not be.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Resource Allocation and Economic Systems
objectives: Explain how market, command and mixed systems answer what to produce, how and for whom.
knowledge: Every allocation answers what, how and for whom.
Market, command and mixed systems answer through different institutions and coordinating mechanisms.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Production Possibilities Curve
objectives: Use a PPC to show trade-offs, efficiency, opportunity cost and growth.
knowledge: Points on the curve are efficient, inside are unused resources, outside are unattainable now.
The shape shows constant, increasing or decreasing opportunity cost; more resources or better technology shift it out.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Comparative Advantage and Trade
objectives: Find absolute and comparative advantage and terms of trade that help both sides.
knowledge: Absolute advantage is more output from the same resources; comparative advantage is the lower opportunity cost.
Specializing by comparative advantage lets both sides consume beyond their own PPCs at terms between their opportunity costs.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Cost-Benefit Analysis
objectives: Compare total costs and benefits, explicit and implicit, to find the best choice.
knowledge: Economic cost includes explicit and implicit costs.
Net benefit (total benefit minus total cost) is largest at the best choice; some choices need totals, others margins.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Marginal Analysis and Consumer Choice
objectives: Use marginal benefit and marginal cost, and marginal utility per dollar, to find the best quantity.
knowledge: With diminishing marginal utility, a consumer maximizes total utility by equalizing marginal utility per dollar across goods with the budget spent.
The best quantity is where marginal benefit equals marginal cost; sunk costs and fixed benefits do not change it. Indifference curves are beyond the course.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Demand
objectives: Explain the law of demand and what shifts demand.
knowledge: The law of demand is a movement along the curve, from income and substitution effects and diminishing marginal utility.
Market demand is the horizontal sum of individual demands; tastes, income, related prices, expectations and the number of buyers shift it.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Supply
objectives: Explain the law of supply and what shifts supply.
knowledge: The law of supply is a movement along the curve.
Market supply is the sum of individual supplies; input prices, technology, related outputs, taxes and subsidies, expectations and the number of sellers shift it.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Price Elasticity of Demand
objectives: Calculate and interpret the price elasticity of demand and the total revenue test.
knowledge: Price elasticity of demand is the percent change in quantity demanded over the percent change in price, read in absolute value: elastic above 1, inelastic below 1, unit elastic at 1.
Elasticity changes along a straight-line demand curve, so slope is not elasticity; the total revenue test links the price change and revenue to elasticity.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Price Elasticity of Supply
objectives: Calculate and interpret the price elasticity of supply.
knowledge: Price elasticity of supply is the percent change in quantity supplied over the percent change in price, with the same benchmarks.
Supply is more elastic with more time and easier input switching.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Other Elasticities
objectives: Use income and cross-price elasticity to classify goods.
knowledge: Income elasticity: positive for normal goods, negative for inferior goods.
Cross-price elasticity: positive for substitutes, negative for complements, near zero for unrelated goods.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Market Equilibrium and Consumer and Producer Surplus
objectives: Find equilibrium and measure consumer, producer and total surplus.
knowledge: Equilibrium clears the market; with no market failure it maximizes total surplus.
Consumer surplus lies under demand above the price; producer surplus above supply below the price.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Market Disequilibrium and Changes in Equilibrium
objectives: Predict shortages, surpluses and the effects of shifts on price, quantity and surplus.
knowledge: Shortages push price up and surpluses push it down until the market clears.
Shifts change price, quantity and surplus; the size of each change depends on the elasticities; double shifts leave one variable indeterminate.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: The Effects of Government Intervention in Markets
objectives: Show the effects of price controls, taxes and subsidies on outcomes, surplus and deadweight loss.
knowledge: Binding ceilings sit below equilibrium and cause shortages; binding floors sit above and cause surpluses.
A per-unit tax or subsidy shifts a curve by its amount; incidence depends on the elasticities; intervention in an efficient market creates deadweight loss.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: International Trade and Public Policy
objectives: Show the effects of opening to trade, tariffs and quotas on a domestic market.
knowledge: At the world price a country imports when it is below the domestic price and exports when above.
A tariff raises the domestic price, cuts imports, raises revenue and creates deadweight loss; quotas cut imports (graphing a quota is beyond the course).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

units.title: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model

topics.title: The Production Function
objectives: Calculate total, marginal and average product and explain diminishing marginal returns.
knowledge: Marginal product is the change in total product from one more unit of an input; average product is total product per unit of input.
Adding a variable input to fixed inputs in the short run eventually brings diminishing marginal returns.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Short-Run Production Costs
objectives: Calculate every short-run cost measure from a table and draw the cost curves.
knowledge: TC = TFC + TVC; fixed cost is the same at every output, including zero.
MC = change in TC over change in output; diminishing returns make MC rise, and MC passes through the minimum of AVC and ATC.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Long-Run Production Costs
objectives: Describe returns to scale and economies and diseconomies of scale on the LRATC curve.
knowledge: In the long run every cost is variable; LRATC shows economies of scale, constant returns and diseconomies.
Minimum efficient scale helps set how many firms a market holds.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); objectives and knowledge in our words from the CED text summarized in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; focus skills from the Course at a Glance tags

topics.title: Types of Profit
objectives: Distinguish accounting, economic and normal profit.
knowledge: Accounting profit = total revenue minus explicit costs; economic profit also subtracts implicit costs.
Normal profit is zero economic profit.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Profit Maximization
objectives: Find the profit-maximizing output with MR = MC and calculate profit.
knowledge: A firm maximizes profit where MR = MC (in a table, the last unit whose MR is at least its MC).
Profit = TR - TC = (P - ATC) × Q.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Firms' Short-Run Decisions to Produce and Long-Run Decisions to Enter or Exit a Market
objectives: Explain the shutdown rule and entry and exit.
knowledge: In the short run a firm produces only if price is at least minimum AVC; fixed costs do not change the output choice.
Economic profit draws entry and losses cause exit, shifting market supply until economic profit is zero.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Perfect Competition
objectives: Draw side-by-side market and firm graphs in the short and long run.
knowledge: The competitive firm is a price taker: its demand is horizontal at the market price, d = MR = AR = P.
Long-run equilibrium is at minimum ATC with zero economic profit.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Introduction to Imperfectly Competitive Markets
objectives: Describe barriers to entry and market power.
knowledge: Barriers to entry let a firm keep market power.
An imperfect competitor faces downward-sloping demand, so its MR lies below demand.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Monopoly
objectives: Draw a monopoly graph: quantity where MR = MC, price from demand, profit, consumer surplus and deadweight loss.
knowledge: A monopolist produces where MR = MC and charges the price on demand above that quantity, on the elastic part of demand.
Natural monopoly: ATC falls over the whole demand range; regulated prices at P = MC (may need a subsidy) or P = ATC (fair return).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Price Discrimination
objectives: Show the effect of perfect price discrimination.
knowledge: A perfectly price-discriminating monopolist has MR equal to demand, so it produces where demand meets MC.
Consumer surplus falls to zero and deadweight loss disappears.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Monopolistic Competition
objectives: Show short-run profit or loss and the long-run tangency in monopolistic competition.
knowledge: Product differentiation gives each firm downward-sloping demand.
Entry or exit shifts each firm's demand until it is tangent to ATC: zero economic profit, excess capacity, price above MC.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge is standard economics in our words (docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; no FRQ 2023-2026; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Oligopoly and Game Theory
objectives: Use payoff matrices to find dominant strategies and Nash equilibria.
knowledge: A dominant strategy is best whatever the rival does; it may not exist and both comparisons settle it.
A Nash equilibrium is a cell where neither player gains by switching alone; there may be one, two or none in pure strategies.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Introduction to Factor Markets
objectives: Explain derived demand and marginal revenue product.
knowledge: The demand for a factor is derived from the demand for the product it makes.
MRP = MP × MR (MP × P for a competitive seller).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Changes in Factor Demand and Factor Supply
objectives: Predict what shifts labor demand and labor supply.
knowledge: Product price or demand and productivity shift labor demand.
Population, preferences and rules on who can work shift labor supply.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Profit-Maximizing Behavior in Perfectly Competitive Factor Markets
objectives: Find the profit-maximizing hiring and the least-cost input mix.
knowledge: A competitive firm hires where MRP = MRC = the market wage; fixed costs do not change hiring.
Least-cost input mix: MP of labor per dollar equals MP of capital per dollar.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Monopsonistic Markets
objectives: Show a monopsonist's hiring and wage.
knowledge: A monopsonist's MFC lies above labor supply; it hires where MRP = MFC and pays the wage read from labor supply.
A minimum wage between the monopsony wage and the competitive wage can raise both wage and employment.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

units.title: Market Failure and the Role of Government

topics.title: Socially Efficient and Inefficient Market Outcomes
objectives: Compare market outcomes with the socially efficient one.
knowledge: The efficient quantity is where marginal social benefit equals marginal social cost.
Any other quantity creates deadweight loss.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Externalities
objectives: Show production and consumption externalities and their corrections.
knowledge: A negative externality makes the market overproduce; a positive one makes it underproduce.
A per-unit tax or subsidy equal to the external cost or benefit at the efficient quantity corrects it; a lump-sum tax does not change MC, price or quantity.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Public and Private Goods
objectives: Classify goods by rivalry and excludability and explain free riding.
knowledge: Goods are rival or nonrival and excludable or nonexcludable.
Public goods invite free riding, so markets underprovide them.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge is standard economics in our words (docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; no FRQ 2023-2026; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: The Effects of Government Intervention in Different Market Structures
objectives: Show government intervention in different market structures.
knowledge: A price ceiling on a monopoly can raise quantity; a minimum wage in a monopsony can raise employment.
Lump-sum and per-unit taxes and subsidies affect firms differently; natural monopolies are regulated.
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge from scoring guidelines and Chief Reader Reports in docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3 (CED text not read; needs-author ced-text)

topics.title: Inequality
objectives: Measure inequality with the Lorenz curve and describe its sources and policies.
knowledge: The Lorenz curve shows the cumulative share of income held by the cumulative share of households; the further it bows from the line of equality, the more unequal.
Taxes can be progressive, proportional or regressive; transfers change the distribution. The Gini coefficient is taught as one measure (needs-author ced-text).
topics.source: Course at a Glance (official title); knowledge is standard economics in our words (docs/apmicro-research/framework.md section 3; no FRQ 2023-2026; needs-author ced-text)

skillsTopics.title: Axes, Variables and Points
objectives: Read and label two axes, plot a point and tell a positive from a negative relationship.
knowledge: Each axis is one variable with its name and units; a point is one pair of values.
A curve rising left to right shows a positive (direct) relationship; falling, a negative (inverse) one.

skillsTopics.title: Slopes and Curve Shapes
objectives: Find a slope as rise over run and describe curved shapes.
knowledge: Slope is the change on the vertical axis over the change on the horizontal axis.
A U-shaped curve falls, bottoms out at its minimum, then rises; a horizontal line has zero slope.

skillsTopics.title: Shifts and Movements Along a Curve
objectives: Tell a movement along a curve from a shift of the curve.
knowledge: A change in the variable on an axis moves along the curve.
A change in anything else shifts the whole curve.

skillsTopics.title: Curves That Cross and Areas
objectives: Read where two curves cross and the areas between curves and lines.
knowledge: Where two curves cross both conditions hold; compare the new crossing with the old on each axis.
An area between curves and lines is a triangle or rectangle: one half base times height, or base times height.

exam.delivery: Hybrid digital: multiple choice in Bluebook; free responses shown in Bluebook and handwritten (graphs drawn by hand) in a paper booklet.

mcq.options: not confirmed (treated as Macro: 5 on exam forms, 4 in the bank; needs-author mcq-options)

types.short: Q2 and Q3, 5 points each, a quarter of the section each, about 12 min each

exam.calculator: Four-function on both sections; Bluebook has a Desmos four-function calculator built in.
